APPROVAL OF MINUTES
  EL MONTE CITY COUNCIL REGULAR MEETING
  OF JANUARY 23, 2024

MEETING JOINTLY AND REGULARLY WITH THE EL MONTE HOUSING AUTHORITY; EL
MONTE PUBLIC FINANCING AUTHORITY; EL MONTE WATER AUTHORITY; EL MONTE
PARKING AUTHORITY; SUCCESSOR AGENCY TO THE FORMER EL MONTE COMMUNITY
REDEVELOPMENT AGENCY; HOUSING SUCCESSOR AGENCY; AND, FROM TIME TO
TIME, SUCH OTHER BODIES OF THE CITY WHOSE MEMBERSHIP IS COMPOSED
EXCLUSIVELY OF THE MEMBERSHIP OF THE CITY COUNCIL

1.  CALL TO ORDER: 6:03 p.m.

2.  ROLL CALL FOR CITY COUNCIL AND AUTHORITY BODIES:

  Jessica Ancona, Mayor/Chair – present
  Dr. Julia Ruedas, Mayor Pro Tem/Authority Member – present
  Marisol Cortez, Councilmember/Authority Member – present
  Martin Herrera, Councilmember/Authority Member – present
  Victoria Martinez Muela, Councilmember/Authority Member – present
  Alma D. Puente, Councilmember/Authority Member – present
  Richard Rojo, Councilmember/Authority Member – present

3.  APPROVAL OF AGENDA:

  WITH THE FOLLOWING EDITS/CHANGES TO THE AGENDA:

  Item 4.1 has been pulled.

4.  CLOSED SESSION:

  The City Council and the various legislative bodies whose membership is composed
  exclusively of the membership of the City Council will attempt to address and complete all
  Closed Session business between 6:00 p.m. and 7:00 p.m. If the City Council completes
  all Closed Session business prior to 7:00 p.m., the City Council will take a short recess
  and commence all Open Session proceedings promptly at 7:00 p.m. In the event the City
  Council is unable to address or complete all agendized Closed Session items by 7:00
  p.m., the City Council will hear all such remaining items toward the end of the meeting,
  immediately following Council Communications. Should any member of the public wish to
  address the City Council on any agendized Closed Session matter, the City Council shall
  allow such person to address the City Council on such matter(s) prior to going into Closed
  Session, provided that all persons wishing to address the Council on an agendized Closed
  Session matter shall (i) call-in or submit a speaker card in the manner prescribed on page
  1 of this agenda, above, prior to the City Council going into closed session; and (ii) be
  subject to a single speaker time allotment of three (3) continuous minutes total per
  speaker to address the City Council on any or all closed session items of business.

  Mayor Ancona invited members of the public to address the City Council on Closed
  Session Items 4.1 through 4.3.

  Mayor Ancona and the City Council recessed into Closed Session at approximately
  6:04 p.m. Mayor Ancona and the City Council reconvened from Closed Session at
  approximately 7:07 p.m. Mayor Ancona and the City Council recessed into Closed
  Session at approximately 8:27 p.m. Mayor Ancon and the City Council reconvened
  from Closed Session at approximately 9:00 p.m.

  4.1  Closed Session Pursuant to Government Code Section 54956.9(d)(1) –

  Item has been pulled.

5.  INVOCATION:  Chaplain. Chaplain Esrom Lempao.

6.  FLAG SALUTE:  Santiago Mendoza, 4th Grade Student from LeGore Elementary

7.  RECOGNITIONS, HONORS AND COMMUNITY INTEREST PRESENTATIONS:

  7.1  Presentation by the City Council to Santiago Mendoza from LeGore Elementary

  7.2  Presentation by the City Council Proclaiming the Month of January 2024 as
  “School Board Recognition Month.” Present

8.  GENERAL PUBLIC COMMENT:

  This time has been set aside for members of the public to directly address the City Council
  on agendized items of business (other than those agendized as public hearing or closed
  session items) or on any other matter of interest to the speaker/caller that is within the
  subject matter jurisdiction of the City Council, the Housing Authority, the Financing
  Authority and/or the Water Authority (collectively, the “Council”). Each speaker/caller will
  be limited to a single allotment of three (3) continuous minutes total to address the Council
  on any or all matters covered by this section. As explained more specifically under the
  Public Hearing portion of this agenda, members of the public wishing to offer comment on
  items of business agendized under the Public Hearing portion of the agenda shall have a
  separate allotment of three (3) continuous minutes per speaker per public hearing item.
  Except as otherwise provided under the Brown Act (Gov. Code Section 54950 et seq.),
  the Council may not deliberate or take action upon any matter not listed on this posted
  agenda but may order that any such matter be placed on the agenda for a subsequent
  meeting. The Council may also direct staff to investigate certain matters for consideration
  at a future meeting. Persons wishing to address the Council on matters covered under
  General Public Comment shall call in or submit a speaker card in the manner prescribed
  on page 1 of this agenda, above, by or before the General Public Comment portion of the
  agenda is closed. The City Council shall be under no obligation to entertain comments
  from speakers/callers who submit cards or call in to speak on matters covered by the
  section after the General Public Comment portion of the agenda is closed.

  Cindy Wu – Thanked the City Council for the recognition.

  Ricardo Padilla - Thanked the City Council for the recognition. Thanked the City Council
  for the SRO Contracts.

  Am Bowes – Provided an update regarding the Coordinating Council meeting.

  Smitty – Addressed the City Council regarding outstanding invoices from the Police

  Julio Ramirez – Spoke about current and former City Councilmembers. Spoke about

  Teodoro Lopez – Request a traffic light on Durfee and Denholm.

  Tony Garcia – Representing the small restaurant businesses. Thanked the City Council

  working on.

  Eric Chen – Invited the City Council to the viewing of a documentary called Come Home
  My Child.

10.  DEMAND RESOLUTION NO. D-702

  A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF EL MONTE, CALIFORNIA,
  ALLOWING CERTAIN CLAIMS AND DEMANDS AND SPECIFYING THE FUNDS OUT
  OF WHICH THE SAME ARE TO BE PAID.

  THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF EL MONTE, CALIFORNIA, DOES RESOLVE AS
  FOLLOWS: SECTION 1. That the attached list of claims and demands totaling
  $7,449,779.01 have been examined by the City Treasurer and that warrant numbers
  1119477 through 1119866, and the payroll period ending December 31, 2023, inclusive
  are hereby allowed in the amounts and ordered paid out of the respective funds as set
  forth.

  m) Councilmember Rojo
  s) Councilmember Puente  7-0

13.  PUBLIC HEARINGS:

  Members of the public wishing to address the Council on any item of business agendized
  under this Public Hearing portion of the agenda are asked to submit a speaker card for
  each Public Hearing item of business they wish to address the Council on. Each speaker
  will be allotted three (3) continuous minutes per Public Hearing item. Members of the
  public are asked to submit speaker cards to the City Clerk or the Sergeant-of-Arms before
  the Council’s approval of the agenda, if possible. The Council is under no obligation to
  recognize a speaker who submits a speaker card for a particular Public Hearing item of
  business after the public comment portion of the public hearing for that item has closed.

  [No Public Hearing Items Agendized for this Council meeting]

18.  COUNCIL COMMUNICATIONS/REPORTS:

  18A.  Mayor Ancona

  18B.  Mayor Pro Tem Dr. Julia Ruedas

  18C.  Councilwoman Cortez

  18D.  Councilman Martin Herrera

  Councilmember Herrera – Spoke to Mr. Tony Garcia regarding the impact Covid
  has had on the restaurants in the City. Asked if the City Council would approve
  giving the City Manager direction on an initiative regarding restaurant week, shop
  local initiative.

  City Manager – A restaurant week for El Monte eateries.

  Mayor Ancona – Agreed that this is a good idea. Maybe have something on a
  quarterly basis.

  6
   City Council Meeting Minutes of January 23, 2024

18E.  Councilwoman Martinez Muela

  Asked the City Manager for an update regarding the Audit for both 2022 and 2023.

  City Manager Martinez – Informed the City Council that the 2022 Audit will be
  brought back to the City Council in late February. The 2023 audit will be submitted
  to the City in May.

  18E.1 Discussion and Direction Regarding Support for El Monte Fillies Softball
  League and Title IX.

  Under Title IX the girls softball teams must be given the same opportunities
  as the boys softball teams. The League would like to enter into an MOU if
  needed with the City. The field needs repair.

  City Manager Martinez – Asked that the League reach out to her to address
  all of their concerns. Will provide the City Council with an update.

  Mayor Ancona – Would like to see this come back.

  18E.2 Update on Policy Proposal from Staff Regarding the Fair and Equitable
  Treatment of Nonprofit Organizations.

  Councilmember Martinez Muela – Spoke about the Women’s Club
  expectation of rent for their space. Would like to know what spaces are out
  there in the community and what other organizations are paying for those
  spaces. Would like for the City Council to create a Policy for a fair and
  equitable treatment across the board for all of the Organizations.

  Assistant City Attorney Pilchen – Provided the City Council with an existing
  Policy for the use by non-profits. Did look at other cities but the subject is
  very broad. Need additional direction.

  Councilmember Martinez Muela – Would like to understand who is utilizing
  City space, what their rent and expectation is. Would like a presentation to
  share with the community.

  Mayor Ancona – Clarified that what is needed is a policy to form some type
  of uniformity.

  City Attorney Olivarez – Advised that the City Attorney’s Office will meet
  with Councilmember Martinez Muela to review the policy they prepare prior
  to bringing back to the City Council.

  18E.3 Discussion and Direction Regarding City Purchase of a Community Garden
  to Add Green Space.

  Councilmember Martinez Muela – Would like a presentation regarding the
  purchase of a community garden.
  Councilmember Herrera – This may be something that could be reviewed
  by the Parks & Recreation Ad Hoc Committee.

  Councilmember Martinez Muela – Would like to agendized on a Parks &
  Recreation Ad Hoc agenda.

  18E.4 Discussion Regarding Creating a Reporting Policy for City Administration
  to Report Monthly to the City Council on Labor Relations, Grievances, and
  Resolutions.

  Councilmember Martinez Muela – Wants to make sure that the City is
  encouraging good labor relations. Requested a report on labor relations,
  grievances and resolutions.

  City Attorney Olivarez – Advised that the City Attorney’s Office may be able
  to prepare a memo addressing some of these matters and could provide

  that to the City Council. If some of these items qualify then they will be
  brought before the City Council in Closed Session.
  Councilmember Puente – Had questions regarding this. Asked if these
  items are items that are already brought to the City Council. Is concerned
  about this.

  City Attorney Olivarez – Advised that some of these items are brought
  before the City Council in Closed Session but not all of them.

  Councilmember Herrera – Concerned with this. This request may be
  something that is beyond the City Council’s role especially regarding
  personnel matters.

  City Attorney Olivarez – Will meet with Councilmember Martinez Muela
  regarding this request and will have an update for the City Council.

  18F.  Councilwoman Puente

  Office located at 11333 Valley Boulevard, El Monte, Monday through Thursday, 7:00 am
  – 5:30 pm. For more information, please call the City Clerk’s Office at 626-580-2016.

  All public meetings and events sponsored or conducted by the City of El Monte are held
  in sites accessible to persons with disabilities. Requests for accommodations may be
  made by calling the office of the City Clerk at (626) 580-2016 at least three (3) working
